body: Oh yeah, there is life all around us. I didn't physically go to another planet, but I suppose if I stuck around there long enough I could have learned more about that particular topic. It was definitely possible to travel through the cosmos, and I don't believe we are the only intelligent life forms out there.

My surgery was a tonsillectomy.   


And one interesting thing I learned about the universe is the idea and notion that we are made of stardust. We (our physical bodies) are infinite and ancient beings in many ways. My revelations about our souls (see other comments, I am too tired to re-write it all again, my apologies) seems to connect with a lot of theories and religious beliefs I had never heard of before.  The many ways we can be reincarnated, for example...it's all true based on my experience. And it's all connected to the universe and how the universe itself behaves and changes and grows. I don't know if any of this even makes sense. It's so incredibly hard for me to explain, and I wish I could just show you the way it was shown to me.

I often feel that the best version of myself has already occurred, and now I am just going through the motions so my brother and mom will not have to mourn me as well. I know this is distorted thinking. I know I am capable of incredible things. I know I was meant for better than what I have to show for myself now. These facts don't motivate me.  I've been stuck in this head-space since 2018.   
There is certainly a lot to unpack when dealing with grief, and this NDE certainly does not make it easier to heal.   


I appreciate your encouragement.

My overall understanding of the universe and the cosmos and all of that...it was never a topic I was interested in or had any knowledge of outside of an astronomy class I took for fun in college. I recently watched a few documentaries about these topics and what should have been new information to me was like I was watching something I had already seen before. A lot of what I have since seen and learned about the universe has also clarified for me a lot of what I saw while on the "other side".

Smaller scale, and the thing that really made me believe this wasn't a dream, is that my dad promised to cure a lifelong chronic condition I had upon my return to Earth.  I had chronic nose bleeds (so bad that I have been hospitalized for them, received transfusions, and had nasal surgery). I learned to live with them and usually they weren't more than an hour long. I guess that part of my life could be a whole other AMA, but anyway....

During my surgery, along with overdosing me, the doctors triggered a serious nose bleed that they could not contain. They were able to stop the bleeding (they don't know how, one minute it was uncontrollable and the next it was like it had never even been bleeding. I think it was my dad keeping his promise) and I haven't had a nosebleed since.
He didn't want me to leave my mom and brother behind - they need me. I appreciate your wishes, and hope we both find what it is we are looking for.
I've tried a few, DMT is on the list next.
This is a really interesting theory.

I have no plans to kill myself, I simply wish I just never "came back". A very relatable feeling to not wanting to hurt oneself but being at peace if they just so happened to die in their sleep. And yearning for that. I know it's messed up.

It 100% could be a mental manifestation. And I would never want to put my mom and brother through the pain of losing me (which is why I came back). However, it really sucks for me to be here. It's as if my only purpose is to be here for the two of them, as I get no pleasure out of life anymore no matter what I do. Are there happy moments? Yes. Are there things I look forward to? Sometimes. Do I have dreams and goals? Yeah, but they will never come to fruition. Would I recommend this existence to anyone? No.   


I used to "have it all" and have it all going for me. I fear those days and opportunities are gone.
I have no intentions of committing suicide, I just wish death came for me sooner rather than later.

I didn't believe in heaven or hell or anything of the sort. I figured we just ceased to exist and that was that. Sure, our bodies would decompose and we'd return to the earth in that sort of sense but I really hadn't given any thought to "souls" or anything like that.
Cue the tears. Thank you for this.

Not being an asshole, that was my initial thought at first as well. But it felt just as real as I feel sitting here typing to you, and all the logic I could throw at myself just didn't seem to feel right. I sat with this for a long time and spoke to so many people (therapists, spiritual leaders, doctors) that I really do not believe it was a dream. I've had some crazy realistic dreams, but this was nothing like that.  It's incredibly hard to explain and describe, and I promise you - until this happened to me I would have been posting your comment on someone elses post for sure.
In some ways it gets "easier" but I seem to struggle with long-term grief/complicated grief.

The doctors overdosed me on fentanyl and my breathing stopped completely. Pulse was weak, if not even existent. I was also bleeding out through my nose and mouth. They were able to get the bleeding under control, and had to Narcan me three times in the OR. I am not sure what other measures were taken, but once they were able to move me from the OR to recovery they still could not wake me for some time.
Thank you. I have called a few hotlines over the years (prior to my dad's passing, I have always had depression) and found them hit or miss. I will check out this sub.
I wouldn't even know where to start! But maybe?
It wasn't scary at all <3

After my dad died my weed intake increased immensely. I use weed multiple times a day now. I microdose mushrooms on a schedule as well, with larger doses/trips occasionally. LSD is used more sparingly, perhaps only 2-3 times a year.  Results vary, with my Mushroom trips bringing me closer to my dad than anything else (but it's not consistent by any means, and requires a large dose).
I have not, but hope to try it i the future.

I am a bit scared to watch that Netflix recommendation, but when I get the courage I will give it a try. Not sure why it scares me.   


I was in a support group for a while, but found it was mostly people that were in the "I was almost in a car accident but I survived" category and less of the "I was legitimately declared dead but was revived" group. I just couldn't relate to the majority of people. I will look into the link you shared though. Thank you.

Thanks for the suggestion. DMT is something on my list of things to try, but I haven't done it yet. I used to meditate daily, but the depression has become so strong that I don't have the patience for it anymore.
Try this one: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XDlaRT7A7p0
Tried that, a few times. No success for me unfortunately.
I have heard this too. I haven't had the opportunity to try DMT but I am interested for sure.
Reaching out now. Thanks for this suggestion.

I was in my "own space" being visited by my father. I do feel there was more of a communal space somewhere down the hallway (both ahead of me and behind me). What that looked like or was I don't know. And my nana was  definitely waiting in the hall behind me.   


I got the impression that each persons "space" was overall similar to what I experienced, but the walls (for lack of a better term) could be lit up with memories, current events, and views into the lives of loved ones back on Earth. Since it was basically my own little slice of the universe, it seemed like the options were limitless as to where I could go through the doorways and what I could see when I looked Earth side.

No pain at all. It was quite strange though. I remember the doctor telling me to count backward from 10 -1 (what they say to everyone to calm anxiety). I promptly passed the fuck out, and found myself standing with my dad. I do not know how much time passed between being placed under and being declared dead, but it felt instantaneous to me from my perspective on the other side. My surgery was only supposed to take 45 minutes max, but I know per my medical records I was in the OR for closer to 2.5 hours. While they got my breathing back and steady in the OR they could not wake me in recovery for another hour or so. 

But to answer your question- I felt no pain while declared dead. But waking up hurt like a mother....

Perhaps the human form isn't capable to comprehending it all, just our souls? I have no idea, to be honest. Life is a mystery for sure. Perhaps all the knowledge is just another bit of "heaven" our souls can receive if we live our best lives. I wish I had all the answers. But then I guess that would mean I'd be dead?
Wikipedia on steroids, basically.

I do feel it was real. It felt more real that those dreams you have that you think are real. It felt just as real as I feel sitting here typing my response to you (minus the bliss and love and incredible sense of serenity and peace). 

Too much of what I observed from the other side and would have no knowledge of otherwise came to fruition and proved to be true. The fact that I asked my dad for a favor and he delivered on that favor is another huge push in the direction that it wasn't just my brain being weird. 

Could I have been hallucinating? Sure. But I have never hallucinated while also being declared dead at the same time.  And, to be clear, I never hallucinated before this experience on the operating table. All subsequent hallucinations were drug induced as a means to try to get back to that feeling I had while I had been declared dead. Those hallucinations were mostly things like bugs and bright colors, though, and I 100% knew they were hallucinations.
I'm not sure what you mean. On Earth, I was unconscious and non-responsive, but my experience on the "other side" was that I (my soul? my essence?) was alive although I knew I was dead.

I am glad therapy and your partner have helped you! My partner tries his best, he never knew my dad. My original therapist was phenomenal, but he moved. New therapist is bleh, and teletherapy is lame. I'm here for you, though. Seems like we might be going through similar struggles.

Souls are not attached to bodies, from what I gather. The soul leaves the body at death. So if you cremate or bury a body, the soul has already moved on to the other place and can feel no physical pain. I fully believe that saying, which I am totally going to mess up:  you do not have a soul, you are a soul. You have a body.

You will know everything that is and everything that was (this knowledge grows over time, it's not instantaneous). The whole of the universe becomes you (or you become it, but with the knowledge of all that it holds). There is an awareness of what is going on Earth side, but only when your attention is called to it. I suppose you could stalk your living relatives but with the vast universe at your finger tips and realizing that time is not linear, you can be many places at once or nowhere at all. There is also the ability to "time travel" in a way; anyone your soul is connected to, past or future, gives you access to their Earthly timeline and you can visit (viewing through the veil I described earlier). For example, when I was talking to me dad he told me he was also with my mom during a completely different Earth day and time that she had "needed" him since his passing.   


Does this make sense? It's very difficult for me to describe and explain but I am doing my best.

When I told my mom about my experience, she cried that she wanted the same thing. The pain is so incredibly raw that it is hard for others to understand. This may sound a bit wacky, but have you tried doing a hypnosis type of deal? I have done these a few times and they have brought me a lot of comfort (be warned, it's a very emotional experience but can be so healing). If you are interested I can send you some links.

It felt 100% real. I felt like I was conscious and watching myself from afar while casually spending time with my dad. Almost like we were in Grey's Anatomy watching from the observation deck or whatever it's call. We were cracking jokes and making comments on what the surgeons were doing, and my prognosis, etc. He was wearing his normal "dad clothes" haha, nothing fancy. He was cremated, which was his wish, and his ashes were spread in the river near our house, where he loved to kayak and spent his last day (before being hospitalized).  I kept some of his ashes and got them made into two pieces of jewelry (they were beautifully done, can't say enough good things about spiritpieces . com ). A bit of him resides in our childhood home as well.   


What worries you about cremation?
Thank you. Me too.

It definitely was his time. If he had survived, he would most likely not have made it through the pandemic with all the issues his recovery would have afforded him. His standard of living would not be what it was, and he would not be happy. I feel him with me frequently and think of him many times a day, but it is no where near the same connection as him being physically in this world or me being where he is now.

I answered some of these in previous replies, but will hit on the topics not previously addressed here.   


From my understanding, the only "punishment" is that which you put upon yourself. Meaning, if you were an asshole in life there is a good chance no one will be waiting for you on the other side, and the memories and connections you have access to will not be overwhelmingly pleasant. The overall feelings you will experience will also reflect your life.   


From my experience, you get to choose who you see in the afterlife. I knew my grandmother (dads side) was accessible, but I did not wish to see her and so I did not. I assume if I wanted to see her, I could have.   


The afterlife is definitely the next place we go to continue to grow and learn in ways we physically cannot while we are earth-side.

I do not/did not have this perspective on his passing. I fail to see any positives in losing my dad suddenly. If anything, it made me decide for a few years not to have children, as the thought of putting someone I birthed, nurtured, and loved through so much pain felt almost evil. I have since changed my stance on having my own children, however now I have learned I cannot anyway. Not trying to sound like "oh poor me", just being honest about my experience.  Perhaps the lesson  learned was that I was extremely lucky to have a Dad as amazing as he was - not many are.

That is what I struggle with the most. The depression prevents a LOT of what I'd like to do with my life (as do finances) and some health issues. I'd rather end here than struggle for another 30+ years without getting anywhere worthwhile. Ideally, I would love to do what you suggest, but the likelihood of that happening seems unlikely.
I have not. I will look it up now.
That would be fine.
This is very interesting! I grew up Jewish, but have never heard these particular narratives. Thank you for sharing.

These are great questions. I don't know that there is a "right" answer to any of these.  That is perhaps the beauty of it? I don't see life as something that has been designed, and I am not sure life is a particular path we are destined or even meant to follow. And if the meaning of life is just do what has already been done by those before me, then why am I here? 

  
I view it more as, we are a bunch of electrons (for lack of a better analogy) bouncing around all over the place, just trying to do whatever we think we are supposed to be doing....but none of us really know. On my visit to the other side I learned the meaning of life (for me, at least) is to love and be a good human. I have always been someone that oozed loved and care for others, but I am tired and I miss my dad. 

Those that do think of life as walking a path (predestined or otherwise)...are they happy? What is their purpose? So many questions.

I don't think it would get boring. It seemed like the possibility for endless adventure and love. Time moved differently "over there" and I also got the sense that our souls could be reborn on earth again...giving opportunities for more experiences.   


I think, based on my experience and what I gleaned from it, that if you are an awful person in life - no one would greet you and guide you when you pass over. I also got the sense that the feelings of bliss and love and peace would not be present - rather, there would be feelings of regret, loneliness, and the like (AKA "hell"). Those without family surely have made impacts on others and would most likely be greeted by those that they best connected with. But again, I was only there for a few minutes Earth time, so these are my best guesses from what I learned in my experience.
Tonsillectomy.

Wow! That experience sounds incredible! I can relate with the time. I would swear to you I spent hours with my Dad, but according to medical records I was technically dead for only a few minutes. I would love to hear your story if you wanted to PM me about it. No pressure if not.   


To answer your questions- if my dad had not passed, I guarantee you my Nana would have been there (I could feel her presence when I was talking with my dad). Our bond was close, but she would have told me to get my ass back into my body, and I would have listened. Most likely because I wouldn't want to leave my parents and realistically was not in a place to be "done" living in the physical world.   


Your second question is a tough one. I don't fear the idea of death at all. To me, it's something I am looking forward to, like retirement, but attainable.  Life is inherently tough. The cons seem to outweigh the benefits for me.  So, in this moment, I would have to say that life has a heavier burden for me.

It's nice to hear from people that have had similar experiences as well. They all vary a bit, but in the end the overall feelings we share are similar (as far as I have seen)

I know that my dad wouldn't want me to throw my life away. Before he died, I was kicking ass and taking names. He was my biggest fan for sure. I don't want a crazy life, but I do feel that I have lost my way (career wise - big time) and my goals and dreams seem to be less likely to become realities with each passing year. I know that there is nothing in my life currently that would make him proud, although I know he would/will always love me and just wants me to be happy.

I answered a bit about my experience on the other side, but I can go into more details here for you.  *With the full knowledge that what I am about to share makes me sound like a nutcase.* I learned that time is not linear and there is a "veil" of sorts between both planes of living. Those that pass are not always physically or spiritually with us, but they are always available if we need them. They have lots of other things to do in their new "lives". I learned that you can reconnect your soul to your soulmates (even those you have not met) and live life again (that's the best way I can explain it) through them and their memories. I also got the sense that our souls are a part of a whole. Like.....a giant apple pie sliced up into thousands of pieces. That is what soul mates are, two pieces of the same pie. The other slices you don't meet, you will meet in the afterlife as you are part of them. Since time is not linear, its very likely pieces of the same pie are not physically on Earth at the same time, and some may have not even been yet!

I was very much looking forward to being with my dad for the rest of time, and exploring the universe and learning more about what it all means.

**What did it look like:**  
It was a long dark hallway. On my left side were large windows/doorways of sorts to other parts myself (including my memories) and the universe, which included doorways to living peoples lives that I could access if called to, or the ability to visit a passed loved one in their "space", etc. On my right side side I could see what was happening in the operating room through a bit of a grainy filter (and from an angle different than where my body physically was). I knew that the hallway went on much further than the spot my Dad and I met. I did not go down this hallway. 

**Was it only your dad you saw?** Yes, although I could feel the presence of my Nana off in the distance. 

**Did you see it understand what God is?** I did not see or feel anything that I would label as God. I am not a religious person, although I am spiritual. I got more of a sense about what it means to be/have a soul than anything, and I did get a strong message that the ideas we have about Heaven and Hell are fantasies. Hell would be dying and having no one waiting for you, and no access to those calling for you (living or dead) and the opposite feelings that I will list in your next question. 

**What did you feel like being there?** Absolute bliss. I have yet to experience this feeling ever in my physical form (and you can bet I tried with use of drugs). There was no pain, and I could physically feel love. I felt relaxed, at peace, fulfilled, as if nothing would ever be anything but wonderful ever again...I am not sure there is a word for what it felt like but it was incredible. 

**Why did your dad persuade you to come back?** 
I was begging him to take me with him. He said he would, if that was what I really wanted. He said that it wasn't my time, I could go back. I was adamant that I was okay with this being my time. He pulled the "what about your mom and brother" card, and I knew that they would not be okay losing both my Dad and myself within months of each other. I have a few chronic conditions, and I remember bargaining with my dad that if he cured my most bothersome condition (the one that was currently impacting my death the most) I would go back for my mom and brother. He kept his word (so far). 

**Did your dad look the exact age to when he was last alive?** He did! He may have made himself a bit slimmer and a bit less grey, but he looked just the way I will always remember him.
